subject: Pricing holdback & interoperability risk — migration economics
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Drew Sanders <drew@lumenex.io>, procurement@lumenex.io
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing holdback & interoperability risk — migration economics

Drew / LumenEx procurement team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table for the migration incentive / holdback structure and call out the interoperability checks we’ll require to release credits. High level: we want to align on economics that protect both sides if runtime compatibility or perf parity takes longer than expected.

Proposal (initial):
- Total migration credit: 15% of first-year committed run-rate (applied as invoice credit).
- Holdback: 10% of that credit retained until two verification gates pass:
  1) Runtime parity: model variant runs on your infra with matching latencies within agreed tolerance for the production workload (measured by our verification harness).
  2) Workload throughput: target sustained request rate/latency for 7 consecutive days (KV-cache and batching profiles enabled).
- Acceleration clause: credits released earlier if both checks pass within a 14-day verification window.
- Rollback / escape: if you choose to roll back within 30 days, we’ll provide a one-time egress/rollback credit (up to 5% of migration credit) to offset validated cutover costs.

Technical/integration checkpoints we’ll need to validate (examples):
- KV-cache warmup hooks and prefix caching preserved for critical request paths.
- Quantization profile acceptance (we’ll run a parity eval on a 5k-sample prompt set).
- Batching latency distribution under your peak QPS.

Attached: lumenex-usage-curve.xlsx with estimated token/throughput profile; draft term sheet (summary) inline below.

Next steps: please confirm if 10% holdback is acceptable, or propose an alternate percentage/milestones. If you prefer, we can map the same economics to discrete milestones (pilot completion, staged rollout, GA).

Thanks — available for a quick sync this afternoon if useful.

—
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0139

From: Drew Sanders <drew@lumenex.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, procurement@lumenex.io
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing holdback & interoperability risk — migration economics

Jonas — thanks for the writeup and for laying out specifics. A few quick reactions from procurement and our infra lead: we appreciate the acceleration clause but the 10% holdback feels high relative to our migration risk — our internal estimate of incremental rollback/operational cost is much lower.

Questions / asks:
- Can you show examples where Redwood has applied a similar holdback? A precedent will help our finance team.
- Would LumenEx accept 5–7% holdback instead, or alternatively, milestone-based releases tied to pilot completion + GA?
- We’ll need explicit SLO definitions for the verification harness (latency percentiles, throughput targets) before committing.

Also tagging procurement@lumenex.io — we’ll need the draft commercial redline for legal review.

Regards,
Drew Sanders
Head of Infrastructure
LumenEx
drew@lumenex.io | +1 (212) 555-0198

Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pricing holdback & interoperability risk — internal align

Internal note — capturing negotiation options before we reply to Drew. Keep this thread internal.

Summary of negotiation posture:
- Move to a 10% headline migration credit but offer a compromise on holdback to 7% (or 5% + a step-release) if LumenEx accepts:
  • Explicit performance SLA band (p50/p90/p99 latency targets) during 14-day verification window.
  • Release schedule: 50% of holdback on pilot pass, remaining 50% on GA after 14 days.
  • If rollback occurs within 30 days, provide up to 5% egress credit (capped).
- Commercial trade: reduced holdback in exchange for a 12-month minimum committed run-rate and a public case study agreement (opt-in).

Operational asks to include in term sheet:
- Detailed verification plan (our harness + their telemetry export).
- Pre-scheduled runtime runbook handoff and contact points (2x engineering hours/week during cutover).
- Acceptance criteria for KV-cache parity and batching latency (we should prescribe the probe queries + dataset).

Suggested language for an internal-facing play:
- "Migration Credits will be issued as invoice credits. A holdback equal to 7% of the Migration Credit will be retained pending the completion of the Verification Gates. The holdback will be released on a two-step schedule: 50% upon Pilot Acceptance, 50% upon GA Acceptance within 14 days of Pilot Acceptance."

I prepared an updated term sheet with these options (attached). Recommend we lead with 7% and be willing to go to 5% with the public-case sweetener.

—
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
[attachments: redwood-delta-term-sheet-v3.pdf]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Drew Sanders <drew@lumenex.io>, procurement@lumenex.io
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 May 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing holdback & interoperability risk — migration economics

Drew, thanks for the quick feedback and for flagging the SLO requirement — totally expected. After an internal review we can accept a compromise that I think balances both concerns:

Final proposal (for your review):
- Migration credit: 15% of first-year committed run-rate.
- Holdback: 7% of the migration credit (down from 10%).
- Release schedule: 50% of the holdback on Pilot Acceptance; remaining 50% on GA Acceptance within 14 days of Pilot Acceptance.
- Acceleration: if both verification gates pass within 7 days, full holdback released immediately.
- Rollback: one-time egress/rollback credit capped at 5% of migration credit if LumenEx elects rollback within 30 days.

We will send a concise SLO appendix that defines the verification harness metrics (p50/p90/p99 latency windows, required throughput baselines, KV-cache hit-rate thresholds) so your legal and infra teams have clear acceptance criteria. I’ve attached the updated term sheet and a DocuSign link to expedite execution. Once the term sheet is signed we’ll schedule a technical kickoff and provision the verification harness environment.

Next steps for you:
- Review and confirm acceptance of the 7% holdback proposal (or propose 5% + public case).
- Legal to review attached term sheet: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/LUM-2028-091
- If accepted, sign via DocuSign and we’ll book the verification window (target week of 6/5).

Thanks — happy to hop on a call Monday to walk the SLO appendix with your infra lead.

—
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference
